subject: Post-call recap: LLM qualification and recommended shortlist for Synthoria
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily@synthetoria.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-19T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: LLM qualification and recommended shortlist for Synthoria

Hi Emily — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap + our recommended next steps and an initial model shortlist based on the use case you described (real-time customer support summarization + policy-check routing).

Call highlights (very high level):
- Target latency requirement: p99 < 300ms for ~256 tokens (you mentioned 200–300ms).
- Expected typical context length: 180–320 tokens, occasional long histories up to ~2k tokens for escalations.
- Estimated concurrency: 80–150 concurrent inference requests during peak.
- Primary success metric: reduction in human-handled escalations + maintained summary fidelity (automated QA).

Redwood recommended shortlist (first-pass):
1) redwood-vicuna-13b-q4 (quantized) — balanced tradeoff: good instruction-following with strong latency on H100 pools. Redwood-verified: seq256 p50~45ms, p90~120ms, p99~290ms; continuous batch TPS ~95 (H100, single model pool).
2) openlm-llama2-13b-chat-q8 — slightly better throughput for chat patterns; p50~60ms, p90~140ms, p99~320ms; TPS ~110 with batching.
3) mistral-instruct-7b-8k — best cost/latency for shorter responses; p50~30ms, p90~80ms, p99~200ms; TPS ~180.

Notes on quality/regressions:
- We'll run the models against your provided eval set (you mentioned a 2.5k prompt holdout). We'll track Rouge/BERTScore-style metrics and a small human-labeled reg check for hallucination risk.
- If you need hard p99 < 200ms at seq256, we should prioritize 7B-class or push to a dedicated H100 pool with lower co-tenancy.

Attached: initial benchmark CSV (synthoria_benchmarks_20260819.csv) and our prompt pack (synthoria_prompt_pack_v1.zip). Also sharing Redwood performance profiles for the models above: https://redwood.ai/perf-profiles/

Immediate next steps I propose:
- You share the sample dataset (S3 link or Drive).
- We run a 72-hour focused benchmark (your three priority prompts + 200 random eval items) and share per-model TPS and latency percentiles.
- Align on pilot scope (Dedicated small pool vs hosted burst) and procurement path.

If this looks right, I’ll schedule the benchmark run with Rishi/Dev tomorrow and send a short mutual action plan for approvals/procurement.

Thanks — Jonas

--
Jonas Weber

From: Emily Park <emily@synthetoria.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: LLM qualification and recommended shortlist for Synthoria

Thanks Jonas — great recap and the shortlist is helpful. A few clarifications from my side: 

1) Latency target: our SLA goal is p99 < 220ms at seq256 for the critical summarize endpoint. For non-critical batch summaries we can accept higher p99s.
2) Throughput: during peak expected traffic we see ~120 concurrent requests; typical payload is chat-like (turns + metadata) with average token generation ~120 tokens per response.
3) Data/sample: here's a pre-sanitized sample we can share for benchmarking: s3://synthoria-samples/2026-08/synthoria_sample_10k.jsonl

A couple of asks: can you send a short table with estimated per-1M-token cost for each shortlisted model (hosted vs dedicated)? Also, we want to confirm whether quantized (q4/q8) models preserve the summarization quality for our prompts — if you can run the eval set against quantized variants in the bench that would be ideal.

Finally, procurement will need a mutual action plan and a rough pilot commitment (we are targeting a 6-week pilot). Procurement contact is procurement@synthoria.ai — I’ll loop them if we have an action plan.

Best,
Emily

Emily Park

Synthoria

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: LLM qualification and recommended shortlist for Synthoria

Hi Emily — quick technical follow-up with concrete perf and cost guidance we can use for the 72-hour bench.

Assumptions I used for the numbers below: seq length = 256 tokens generated, batcher active with 8–16ms batching latency, model loaded with KV cache, H100 (pinned Dedicated pool) vs A100 (standard hosted).

A. Preliminary latency/TPS snapshots (approx):
- redwood-vicuna-13b-q4 (H100, Dedicated small pool): p50 45ms / p90 120ms / p99 290ms; median token throughput ~620 tok/s (approx per-GPU stream) => for typical 120-token response that maps to ~5 responses/s per stream; continuous batching gives ~95–110 requests/s in our pool sizing tests.
- openlm-llama2-13b-chat-q8 (H100): p50 60ms / p90 140ms / p99 320ms; TPS slightly higher due to q8 math optimizations ~700 tok/s.
- mistral-instruct-7b-8k (A100 or H100): p50 30ms / p90 80ms / p99 200ms; TPS ~1,100 tok/s — best fit if you need hard p99 headroom.

B. Cost guidance (very rough, ballpark per 1M generated tokens):
- redwood-vicuna-13b-q4 (hosted): ~$27–35 / 1M tokens; (dedicated amortized): ~$18–25 / 1M tokens depending on committed hours.
- openlm-llama2-13b-chat-q8: hosted ~$30–38 / 1M tokens; dedicated ~$20–28 / 1M tokens.
- mistral-instruct-7b-8k: hosted ~$14–20 / 1M tokens; dedicated ~$9–14 / 1M tokens.

C. Quality/regression plan:
- We should evaluate quantized variants side-by-side (q4 vs q8) on your labeled holdout (the 2.5k). I suggest we compute: summary ROUGE/F1, hallucination flag rate, and a small human spot-check of 200 items for critical intents. If the regression vs FP baseline is < 3% on the key metrics we can consider q4 acceptable.

D. Pilot options:
- Option A: Hosted + reserved concurrency for 6 weeks (fastest).
- Option B: Dedicated small H100 pool for 6 weeks (predictable p99 and isolation) — aligns with procurement ask.

I’ve attached a CSV with the raw run snapshots we used for the shortlist (synthoria_benchmarks_20260819.csv) and I dropped a quick prompt pack link to shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xSynthe-Promptsets-Share

If you confirm the SLA target (p99 220ms at seq256) and the pilot preference (hosted vs dedicated), we’ll schedule the 72-hour run and deliver the full per-model report + token-cost delta analysis.

Thanks — Rishi

--
